dutch: Ik werk op de servicedesk.
english: I work on the service desk.
scenario: You meet a colleague from another department for the first time. Tell them that you work on the service desk.
cue: You meet a colleague from another department for the first time. Tell them that you work on the service desk.
grammar: Present statement. The first constituent is Ik; werk is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. A normal declarative main clause has one first constituent and then its finite verb. The subject can be that first constituent. Other phrases can appear inside the verb bracket. Op de servicedesk identifies your team or workplace, rather than a task you are currently troubleshooting.
variation: Onze nieuwe collega helpt met de telefoonmeldingen.

dutch: Ik ondersteun gebruikers bij hun dagelijkse computerproblemen.
english: I support users with their everyday computer problems.
scenario: During an informal introduction, a colleague asks what kind of support you provide. Explain that you help users with everyday computer problems.
cue: During an informal introduction, a colleague asks what kind of support you provide. Explain that you help users with everyday computer problems.
grammar: Present statement. The first constituent is Ik; ondersteun is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. A normal declarative main clause has one first constituent and then its finite verb. The subject can be that first constituent. Other phrases can appear inside the verb bracket. Gebruikers is the plural object; hun refers to those users. Bij introduces the situations in which you support them.
variation: Na de introductie ken ik de namen van mijn teamleden.

dutch: Mijn eerste aanspreekpunt is de teamleider.
english: My first point of contact is the team leader.
scenario: You have just joined the support team. Tell a colleague who your first point of contact is.
cue: You have just joined the support team. Tell a colleague who your first point of contact is.
grammar: Present statement. The first constituent is Mijn eerste aanspreekpunt; is is the finite main verb and Mijn eerste aanspreekpunt is its subject. A normal declarative main clause has one first constituent and then its finite verb. The subject can be that first constituent. Other phrases can appear inside the verb bracket. Aanspreekpunt is a het-word, but mijn replaces the article. The complete phrase Mijn eerste aanspreekpunt is one subject constituent.
variation: Wie begeleidt de stagiairs op de servicedesk?

dutch: Welke collega's werken aan dezelfde meldingen als ik?
english: Which colleagues work on the same support requests as I do?
scenario: You are learning how work is shared. Ask which colleagues deal with the same support requests as you.
cue: You are learning how work is shared. Ask which colleagues deal with the same support requests as you.
grammar: Question word and inversion. The first question constituent is Welke collega's; werken is the finite verb. A question word/phrase comes first, then the finite verb and subject. In a subject question the question phrase itself is the subject, so no extra subject is needed. The question phrase Welke collega's is itself the plural subject. Aan introduces the requests being worked on; als ik completes the comparison.
variation: Ik heb vroeger in een ondersteuningsteam gewerkt.

dutch: Ben jij mijn begeleider op de servicedesk?
english: Are you my mentor on the service desk?
scenario: On your first day, you meet a colleague who may be your assigned mentor. Ask them informally whether that is their role.
cue: On your first day, you meet a colleague who may be your assigned mentor. Ask them informally whether that is their role.
grammar: Yes/no question. The finite verb Ben comes before subject jij. The finite verb starts the yes/no question, followed by the subject. With subject je/jij after the verb, an ordinary present stem loses its -t; formal u does not follow that rule. Ben is the inverted present form before jij. Begeleider means the person guiding your onboarding here.
variation: Mijn collega beheert de gebruikersaccounts.

dutch: Ons team beheert de computers van de medewerkers.
english: Our team manages the employees' computers.
scenario: A new colleague asks what your team is responsible for. Explain that it manages the employees' computers.
cue: A new colleague asks what your team is responsible for. Explain that it manages the employees' computers.
grammar: Present statement. The first constituent is Ons team; beheert is the finite main verb and Ons team is its subject. A normal declarative main clause has one first constituent and then its finite verb. The subject can be that first constituent. Other phrases can appear inside the verb bracket. Team is a singular het-word, so use ons team. The employees own/use the computers; they are not the subject managing them.
variation: We leren de nieuwe teamleden kennen.

dutch: Vanaf maandag werk ik samen met de systeembeheerders.
english: From Monday onward, I will work with the systems administrators.
scenario: You are explaining a confirmed change to your work assignment. Tell a colleague that you will start working with the systems administrators on Monday.
cue: You are explaining a confirmed change to your work assignment. Tell a colleague that you will start working with the systems administrators on Monday.
grammar: Fronted phrase and V2. The first constituent is Vanaf maandag; werk is the finite main verb and ik is its subject. The complete time, place or object phrase is one first constituent. The finite verb follows it, then the subject: second position means a constituent, not the second written word. Vanaf means from that time onward. A present verb with a future starting point can describe a confirmed arrangement.
variation: Ik werk vanaf maandag samen met de systeembeheerders.

dutch: Ik ken nog niet iedereen van het ondersteuningsteam.
english: I do not know everyone in the support team yet.
scenario: A colleague assumes you know the whole support team. Explain that you have not yet become acquainted with every member.
cue: A colleague assumes you know the whole support team. Explain that you have not yet become acquainted with every member.
grammar: Niet, geen and scope. The first constituent is Ik; ken is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. Geen negates an indefinite noun phrase or an uncountable amount. Niet negates a verb/state or another specific constituent. Nog niet means not yet; niet meer means no longer. The position depends on the intended scope. Nog niet iedereen means not everyone yet; it does not mean you know no one. Kennen concerns familiarity with people.
variation: Ik zal me tijdens het teamoverleg voorstellen.

dutch: Ik heb mijn nieuwe collega's gisteren ontmoet.
english: I met my new colleagues yesterday.
scenario: A colleague asks about yesterday's onboarding. Say that you met your new colleagues then.
cue: A colleague asks about yesterday's onboarding. Say that you met your new colleagues then.
grammar: Perfect and verb bracket. The first constituent is Ik; heb is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The finite auxiliary is in the main-clause verb position. Its object, pronouns and other phrases can stand before the participle that closes the bracket. Auxiliary choice depends on the actual verb and meaning. Nieuwe identifies recently joined colleagues in this context. Heb ontmoet reports the completed meeting; it does not claim you already know them well.
variation: Kan ik op mijn eerste werkdag met een collega meelopen?

dutch: Ik stel me graag aan het ondersteuningsteam voor.
english: I would like to introduce myself to the support team.
scenario: You are attending the support team's meeting for the first time. Politely indicate that you would like to introduce yourself to the group.
cue: You are attending the support team's meeting for the first time. Politely indicate that you would like to introduce yourself to the group.
grammar: Reflexive construction. The first constituent is Ik; stel is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The reflexive pronoun belongs to the verb's subject: ik–me, je–je, hij/zij–zich, we–ons. A separable reflexive verb still splits in a main clause. Stel me voor is reflexive and separable. Graag softens your introduction; it does not claim that you have already introduced yourself.
variation: Gisteren stelde de teamleider mij aan de collega's voor.

dutch: Waar vind ik de werkplekken voor het ondersteuningsteam?
english: Where can I find the workstations for the support team?
scenario: You are new in the building. Ask a colleague where the support team's workstations are located.
cue: You are new in the building. Ask a colleague where the support team's workstations are located.
grammar: Question word and inversion. The first question constituent is Waar; vind is the finite verb. A question word/phrase comes first, then the finite verb and subject. In a subject question the question phrase itself is the subject, so no extra subject is needed. Waar asks for location. Vind before subject ik is the ordinary ik form; no extra kan is required in Dutch.
variation: Waar staat de printer voor bezoekers?

dutch: Is deze vergaderzaal vrij voor een ondersteuningsgesprek?
english: Is this meeting room available for a support call?
scenario: You need a room for a support call. Ask a colleague whether this meeting room is available for that purpose.
cue: You need a room for a support call. Ask a colleague whether this meeting room is available for that purpose.
grammar: Yes/no question. The finite verb Is comes before subject deze vergaderzaal. The finite verb starts the yes/no question, followed by the subject. With subject je/jij after the verb, an ordinary present stem loses its -t; formal u does not follow that rule. Vrij means unoccupied/available in this context, not free of charge. Voor names its intended use.
variation: Is de stille werkruimte vandaag beschikbaar?

dutch: Waar staat het reservetoetsenbord?
english: Where is the spare keyboard?
scenario: A user's keyboard needs replacing. Ask your colleague where the spare keyboard is kept.
cue: A user's keyboard needs replacing. Ask your colleague where the spare keyboard is kept.
grammar: Question word and inversion. The first question constituent is Waar; staat is the finite verb. A question word/phrase comes first, then the finite verb and subject. In a subject question the question phrase itself is the subject, so no extra subject is needed. Het reservetoetsenbord is the subject. Staan is a natural location verb for equipment kept ready for use.
variation: De vergaderzaal bevindt zich naast de receptie.

dutch: Mag ik deze gedeelde werkplek vandaag gebruiken?
english: May I use this shared workstation today?
scenario: You see a shared workstation and want to use it today. Ask a colleague for permission rather than assuming it is assigned to you.
cue: You see a shared workstation and want to use it today. Ask a colleague for permission rather than assuming it is assigned to you.
grammar: Modal request or permission question. The finite verb Mag comes before subject ik. The finite modal comes before the subject. The requested action stays an infinitive without te. Whether this asks about ability, permission or willingness depends on the actual modal and context. Werkplek is a de-word: deze gedeelde werkplek. Mag asks permission; physical availability alone does not establish it.
variation: Mag ik deze vrije werkplek gebruiken?

dutch: Welke ingang gebruiken we buiten de kantooruren?
english: Which entrance do we use outside office hours?
scenario: You may need to enter the building for scheduled work outside office hours. Ask a colleague which entrance the team uses then.
cue: You may need to enter the building for scheduled work outside office hours. Ask a colleague which entrance the team uses then.
grammar: Question word and inversion. The first question constituent is Welke ingang; gebruiken is the finite verb. A question word/phrase comes first, then the finite verb and subject. In a subject question the question phrase itself is the subject, so no extra subject is needed. Welke ingang is the object question phrase, while we is the subject. Buiten de kantooruren is common Belgian phrasing for outside office hours.
variation: Bij de ingang staat een kast voor bezoekerspassen.

dutch: Er is een stille ruimte voor vertrouwelijke gesprekken.
english: There is a quiet room for confidential conversations.
scenario: A colleague needs privacy for a confidential conversation. Explain that a quiet room is available for that purpose.
cue: A colleague needs privacy for a confidential conversation. Explain that a quiet room is available for that purpose.
grammar: Existential or referring er. The first constituent is Er; is is the finite main verb and een stille ruimte is its subject. Er can introduce the existence/appearance of something, or combine with a preposition to refer back to a thing. These are different functions; agreement and meaning depend on the actual sentence. Er introduces the existence of een stille ruimte. The room is grammatically the singular subject, despite appearing after is.
variation: Vanmorgen zocht ik naar een rustige vergaderzaal.

dutch: Kun je me tonen waar het materiaal voor nieuwe medewerkers ligt?
english: Can you show me where the equipment for new employees is?
scenario: You need equipment for a new employee but do not know where it is stored. Ask a colleague informally to show you.
cue: You need equipment for a new employee but do not know where it is stored. Ask a colleague informally to show you.
grammar: Modal request or permission question. The finite verb Kun comes before subject je. The finite modal comes before the subject. The requested action stays an infinitive without te. Whether this asks about ability, permission or willingness depends on the actual modal and context. Me is the person to be shown. The embedded location question ends in ligt; materiaal is an uncountable het-word.
variation: Vraag de receptionist naar een bezoekerspas.

dutch: Naast de receptie ligt de lijst met interne telefoonnummers.
english: The list of internal telephone numbers is next to reception.
scenario: A new colleague asks for internal phone numbers. Tell them where the physical list is located.
cue: A new colleague asks for internal phone numbers. Tell them where the physical list is located.
grammar: Fronted phrase and V2. The first constituent is Naast de receptie; ligt is the finite main verb and de lijst met interne telefoonnummers. is its subject. The complete time, place or object phrase is one first constituent. The finite verb follows it, then the subject: second position means a constituent, not the second written word. The whole location phrase is first. Ligt suits a list lying on a surface; de lijst is the subject.
variation: De lijst met interne telefoonnummers ligt naast de receptie.

dutch: Ik heb de werkplek voor de nieuwe medewerker klaargemaakt.
english: I have prepared the workstation for the new employee.
scenario: Your team leader asks about the incoming employee's workstation. Report that you have finished preparing it.
cue: Your team leader asks about the incoming employee's workstation. Report that you have finished preparing it.
grammar: Perfect and verb bracket. The first constituent is Ik; heb is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The finite auxiliary is in the main-clause verb position. Its object, pronouns and other phrases can stand before the participle that closes the bracket. Auxiliary choice depends on the actual verb and meaning. Klaargemaakt is a separable participle. The completed preparation does not claim that the employee has already arrived.
variation: Ik weet niet welke ingang de bezoekers gebruiken.

dutch: Ik weet nog niet waar we defect materiaal bewaren.
english: I do not yet know where we keep faulty equipment.
scenario: A colleague asks you to put faulty equipment away. Explain that you do not yet know the designated storage location.
cue: A colleague asks you to put faulty equipment away. Explain that you do not yet know the designated storage location.
grammar: Main and subordinate clause. The first constituent is Ik; weet is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The main clause retains its own finite-verb position. The conjunction introduces a separate clause whose subject and other material precede its finite verb or verb group. The conjunction's meaning must fit the situation. Waar introduces an embedded location question with final bewaren. Defect materiaal is faulty equipment, not a diagnosis of its cause.
variation: De lockers staan tegenover de personeelsingang.

dutch: Ik ben vanochtend het eerste aanspreekpunt voor gebruikers.
english: I am the first point of contact for users this morning.
scenario: Your team is confirming today's coverage. Tell a colleague that you are the first person users should contact this morning.
cue: Your team is confirming today's coverage. Tell a colleague that you are the first person users should contact this morning.
grammar: Present statement. The first constituent is Ik; ben is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. A normal declarative main clause has one first constituent and then its finite verb. The subject can be that first constituent. Other phrases can appear inside the verb bracket. Vanochtend limits the assignment to this morning. Aanspreekpunt refers to a contact role, not a physical desk.
variation: Ik ben tot de middag bereikbaar via de servicedesk.

dutch: Na twee uur heb ik tijd voor nieuwe meldingen.
english: After two o'clock, I have time for new support requests.
scenario: A colleague asks when you can handle additional requests today. Say that you have time for them after two o'clock.
cue: A colleague asks when you can handle additional requests today. Say that you have time for them after two o'clock.
grammar: Fronted phrase and V2. The first constituent is Na twee uur; heb is the finite main verb and ik is its subject. The complete time, place or object phrase is one first constituent. The finite verb follows it, then the subject: second position means a constituent, not the second written word. Na twee uur means after two o'clock in this schedule context, not after a two-hour duration.
variation: Ik heb na twee uur tijd voor nieuwe meldingen.

dutch: Ik ben tijdens de opleiding niet telefonisch bereikbaar.
english: I am not reachable by phone during the training.
scenario: You are about to attend training. Tell your team that phone calls will not reach you during that period.
cue: You are about to attend training. Tell your team that phone calls will not reach you during that period.
grammar: Niet, geen and scope. The first constituent is Ik; ben is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. Geen negates an indefinite noun phrase or an uncountable amount. Niet negates a verb/state or another specific constituent. Nog niet means not yet; niet meer means no longer. The position depends on the intended scope. Niet negates telephone reachability. The sentence does not rule out every other contact channel.
variation: Bent u na de middag bereikbaar voor een kort gesprek?

dutch: Kun je de servicedesk tot mijn terugkomst ondersteunen?
english: Can you support the service desk until I return?
scenario: You must step away temporarily. Ask a colleague informally to support the service desk until you return.
cue: You must step away temporarily. Ask a colleague informally to support the service desk until you return.
grammar: Modal request or permission question. The finite verb Kun comes before subject je. The finite modal comes before the subject. The requested action stays an infinitive without te. Whether this asks about ability, permission or willingness depends on the actual modal and context. Tot mijn terugkomst gives an ending condition for the requested support, not a permanent reassignment.
variation: Ik ben tijdens de opleiding niet beschikbaar voor telefoontjes.

dutch: Bent u morgen tussen negen en tien beschikbaar?
english: Are you available tomorrow between nine and ten?
scenario: You are arranging a support appointment with a customer you address formally. Ask whether tomorrow between nine and ten is available.
cue: You are arranging a support appointment with a customer you address formally. Ask whether tomorrow between nine and ten is available.
grammar: Yes/no question. The finite verb Bent comes before subject u. The finite verb starts the yes/no question, followed by the subject. With subject je/jij after the verb, an ordinary present stem loses its -t; formal u does not follow that rule. Formal u keeps bent in inversion. Tussen ... en defines one time window; it is not a choice between two appointments.
variation: Ik heb mijn afwezigheid aan de planning doorgegeven.

dutch: Ik heb mijn werktijden in de gedeelde agenda gezet.
english: I have put my working hours in the shared calendar.
scenario: A colleague asks where to check your availability. Explain that you have entered your working hours in the shared calendar.
cue: A colleague asks where to check your availability. Explain that you have entered your working hours in the shared calendar.
grammar: Perfect and verb bracket. The first constituent is Ik; heb is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The finite auxiliary is in the main-clause verb position. Its object, pronouns and other phrases can stand before the participle that closes the bracket. Auxiliary choice depends on the actual verb and meaning. Agenda means a calendar here, not the meeting's list of topics. Gezet is the irregular participle of zetten.
variation: Kun je mijn telefoontjes tot tien uur overnemen?

dutch: Ik laat het je weten als mijn beschikbaarheid verandert.
english: I will let you know if my availability changes.
scenario: You have just agreed on your availability with a colleague. Promise to notify them if that availability changes.
cue: You have just agreed on your availability with a colleague. Promise to notify them if that availability changes.
grammar: Main and subordinate clause. The first constituent is Ik; laat is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The main clause retains its own finite-verb position. The conjunction introduces a separate clause whose subject and other material precede its finite verb or verb group. The conjunction's meaning must fit the situation. Het refers to the update and je is the receiver. Als introduces a condition; this does not predict that the schedule will change.
variation: Ik laat je weten zodra ik weer beschikbaar ben.

dutch: Vanmorgen was ik even niet aan mijn bureau.
english: This morning I was briefly away from my desk.
scenario: A colleague tried to reach you earlier this morning. Explain that you were briefly away from your desk then.
cue: A colleague tried to reach you earlier this morning. Explain that you were briefly away from your desk then.
grammar: Simple past. The first constituent is Vanmorgen; was is the finite main verb and ik is its subject. The finite past form occupies the ordinary main-clause verb position. Its number agrees with the subject. The past event belongs to the context supplied, not automatically to every repeated or present situation. Was reports a past state. Even limits the absence to a short period rather than the whole morning.
variation: Tijdens het eerste telefoontje was ik al in een ander gesprek.

dutch: Deze week heb ik minder tijd voor extra taken dan vorige week.
english: This week I have less time for extra tasks than last week.
scenario: A colleague asks you to take on additional work. Explain that you have less spare task time this week than you did last week.
cue: A colleague asks you to take on additional work. Explain that you have less spare task time this week than you did last week.
grammar: Comparison or quantity. The first constituent is Deze week; heb is the finite main verb and ik is its subject. The comparison/quantity phrase names the relevant degree or amount. A Dutch comparative commonly uses dan for the comparison, while the positive equality pattern uses even ... als. Minder tijd compares an uncountable amount; dan introduces the comparison. Deze week is a time phrase, not the grammatical subject.
variation: Mijn werkdag begint een halfuur later dan die van jou.

dutch: Ik zal mijn overdracht voor het einde van mijn dienst voorbereiden.
english: I will prepare my handover before the end of my shift.
scenario: Your colleague will take over after your shift. Promise to prepare the handover before your shift ends.
cue: Your colleague will take over after your shift. Promise to prepare the handover before your shift ends.
grammar: Future intention or commitment. The first constituent is Ik; zal is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The finite future/intention verb occupies the main-clause verb position; the intended action is a bare infinitive. A future commitment is not a report of completed work. Voor het einde sets a deadline. Voorbereiden remains joined after zal; the sentence is a commitment, not a completion report.
variation: Laten we onze beschikbaarheid voor morgen afstemmen.

dutch: Wanneer kunnen we onze pauzes verdelen?
english: When can we arrange our breaks?
scenario: The support team needs continuous coverage. Ask a colleague when you can agree how to stagger your breaks.
cue: The support team needs continuous coverage. Ask a colleague when you can agree how to stagger your breaks.
grammar: Question word and inversion. The first question constituent is Wanneer; kunnen is the finite verb. A question word/phrase comes first, then the finite verb and subject. In a subject question the question phrase itself is the subject, so no extra subject is needed. Onze refers to plural pauzes. Verdelen means distribute/arrange them across the group here, not take all breaks at once.
variation: Ik neem mijn pauze na het huidige gesprek.

dutch: Ik neem mijn lunchpauze na de gebruikersafspraak.
english: I will take my lunch break after the user appointment.
scenario: A teammate asks about your lunch plans. Explain that your lunch break will follow the appointment with a user.
cue: A teammate asks about your lunch plans. Explain that your lunch break will follow the appointment with a user.
grammar: Present statement. The first constituent is Ik; neem is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. A normal declarative main clause has one first constituent and then its finite verb. The subject can be that first constituent. Other phrases can appear inside the verb bracket. The present expresses an arranged sequence in this context. It does not imply that the user appointment is already finished.
variation: Kun je de telefoon opnemen terwijl ik even pauze neem?

dutch: Kun je de nieuwe collega bij de lunch betrekken?
english: Can you include the new colleague at lunch?
scenario: A newcomer is joining the team today. Ask another colleague informally to include that person when the group has lunch.
cue: A newcomer is joining the team today. Ask another colleague informally to include that person when the group has lunch.
grammar: Modal request or permission question. The finite verb Kun comes before subject je. The finite modal comes before the subject. The requested action stays an infinitive without te. Whether this asks about ability, permission or willingness depends on the actual modal and context. Betrekken bij means include in. The new colleague receives inclusion rather than an assigned support task.
variation: We hebben geen gezamenlijke lunchpauze op drukke dagen.

dutch: Ik heb nog geen pauze genomen sinds het eerste telefoontje.
english: I have not taken a break since the first phone call.
scenario: A teammate asks whether you have rested during the busy shift. Explain that you have not taken a break since the first call.
cue: A teammate asks whether you have rested during the busy shift. Explain that you have not taken a break since the first call.
grammar: Perfect and verb bracket. The first constituent is Ik; heb is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The finite auxiliary is in the main-clause verb position. Its object, pronouns and other phrases can stand before the participle that closes the bracket. Auxiliary choice depends on the actual verb and meaning. Heb ... genomen is the perfect of nemen. Nog geen means not any break yet; sinds identifies the starting point of that period.
variation: Tijdens mijn pauze blijft de servicedesk bereikbaar.

dutch: Ik kom terug zodra mijn pauze voorbij is.
english: I will return as soon as my break is over.
scenario: Before taking your break, tell the colleague covering you that you will return as soon as it ends.
cue: Before taking your break, tell the colleague covering you that you will return as soon as it ends.
grammar: Main and subordinate clause. The first constituent is Ik; kom is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The main clause retains its own finite-verb position. The conjunction introduces a separate clause whose subject and other material precede its finite verb or verb group. The conjunction's meaning must fit the situation. Zodra gives a future time condition with final is. The main present kom can express the promised return.
variation: Ik heb met mijn collega een later pauzemoment afgesproken.

dutch: Tijdens de middagpauze bespreken we geen vertrouwelijke gebruikersgegevens.
english: We do not discuss confidential user details during the lunch break.
scenario: You are explaining a team privacy practice to a colleague. Say that confidential user details are not discussed over lunch.
cue: You are explaining a team privacy practice to a colleague. Say that confidential user details are not discussed over lunch.
grammar: Fronted phrase and V2. The first constituent is Tijdens de middagpauze; bespreken is the finite main verb and we is its subject. The complete time, place or object phrase is one first constituent. The finite verb follows it, then the subject: second position means a constituent, not the second written word. Geen negates the plural indefinite gegevens. This describes a privacy practice, not a refusal to discuss all work topics.
variation: We bespreken tijdens de middagpauze geen vertrouwelijke gebruikersgegevens.

dutch: Gisteren bleef ik tijdens de pauze bij de nieuwe medewerker.
english: Yesterday I stayed with the new employee during the break.
scenario: A colleague asks how you helped the new employee settle in yesterday. Say that you stayed with them during the break.
cue: A colleague asks how you helped the new employee settle in yesterday. Say that you stayed with them during the break.
grammar: Simple past. The first constituent is Gisteren; bleef is the finite main verb and ik is its subject. The finite past form occupies the ordinary main-clause verb position. Its number agrees with the subject. The past event belongs to the context supplied, not automatically to every repeated or present situation. Bleef is singular past of blijven. Bij describes being with the employee, not working on a support ticket.
variation: Tijdens de lunch bespraken we de eerste werkweek.

dutch: Laten we de pauze om beurten nemen.
english: Let's take our break in turns.
scenario: You and a colleague both need a break while support coverage must continue. Suggest taking the break in turns.
cue: You and a colleague both need a break while support coverage must continue. Suggest taking the break in turns.
grammar: Joint proposal. The first constituent is Laten; Laten is the finite main verb and we is its subject. Laten we invites the speaker and others to act together. The requested action is a bare infinitive; the proposal does not report that the action has already been completed. Om beurten is a fixed expression meaning in turns. It is not an om te infinitive phrase.
variation: Een korte wandeling helpt me om daarna weer geconcentreerd te werken.

dutch: Is er nog plaats aan jullie lunchtafel?
english: Is there still room at your lunch table?
scenario: You would like to join colleagues for lunch. Ask informally whether there is still room at their table.
cue: You would like to join colleagues for lunch. Ask informally whether there is still room at their table.
grammar: Yes/no question. The finite verb Is comes before subject plaats aan jullie lunchtafel?. The finite verb starts the yes/no question, followed by the subject. With subject je/jij after the verb, an ordinary present stem loses its -t; formal u does not follow that rule. Existential er introduces available room. Nog means still; jullie is a plural possessive referring to the colleagues.
variation: Neem jij vandaag de eerste pauze?

dutch: Ik gebruik de pauze om even weg van het scherm te zijn.
english: I use the break to spend a little time away from the screen.
scenario: A colleague asks why you step away from your computer during breaks. Explain that you use the break to spend a short time away from the screen.
cue: A colleague asks why you step away from your computer during breaks. Explain that you use the break to spend a short time away from the screen.
grammar: Purpose or intended action. The first constituent is Ik; gebruik is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. Om introduces an infinitive phrase with te. Its object can come before the infinitive; with a separable verb te stands between its particle and verb. This is not a second finite clause. Om te zijn names the purpose; even means briefly. It does not say that you leave the building.
variation: Ik zal de nieuwe collega bij de lunch betrekken.

dutch: Ik heb ervaring met gebruikersondersteuning op afstand.
english: I have experience with remote user support.
scenario: A colleague asks about your previous support experience. Explain that you have worked with remote user support.
cue: A colleague asks about your previous support experience. Explain that you have worked with remote user support.
grammar: Present statement. The first constituent is Ik; heb is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. A normal declarative main clause has one first constituent and then its finite verb. The subject can be that first constituent. Other phrases can appear inside the verb bracket. Ervaring met is a fixed combination. This is a present statement of experience, not an assertion that every remote problem is familiar.
variation: Ik beheer vooral accounts en toegangsrechten.

dutch: Ik wil de interne toepassingen beter leren kennen.
english: I want to get to know the internal applications better.
scenario: You are discussing your learning goals with a teammate. Say that you want to become more familiar with the internal applications.
cue: You are discussing your learning goals with a teammate. Say that you want to become more familiar with the internal applications.
grammar: Modal and final infinitive. The first constituent is Ik; wil is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The modal is finite and occupies the main-clause verb position. The other action is an infinitive without te, normally toward the end of its clause. Leren kennen describes gaining familiarity. Wanting to learn is not the same as already knowing how each application works.
variation: Ik ken deze toepassing nog niet goed.

dutch: Ik ken deze werkwijze niet uit mijn vorige functie.
english: I am not familiar with this procedure from my previous role.
scenario: A colleague asks whether a procedure is familiar from your earlier job. Explain that you did not encounter it in that role.
cue: A colleague asks whether a procedure is familiar from your earlier job. Explain that you did not encounter it in that role.
grammar: Niet, geen and scope. The first constituent is Ik; ken is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. Geen negates an indefinite noun phrase or an uncountable amount. Niet negates a verb/state or another specific constituent. Nog niet means not yet; niet meer means no longer. The position depends on the intended scope. Kennen uit names the source of familiarity. Vorige means previous, not necessarily a different employer.
variation: Ik heb eerder gebruikers op afstand ondersteund.

dutch: Ik voel me nog onzeker bij complexe storingen.
english: I still feel uncertain when dealing with complex disruptions.
scenario: Your mentor asks where you need support. Explain that complex disruptions still make you feel unsure.
cue: Your mentor asks where you need support. Explain that complex disruptions still make you feel unsure.
grammar: Reflexive construction. The first constituent is Ik; voel is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The reflexive pronoun belongs to the verb's subject: ik–me, je–je, hij/zij–zich, we–ons. A separable reflexive verb still splits in a main clause. Voel me describes your feeling; gevoel would be a noun. Nog signals that this uncertainty continues for now.
variation: Ik wil onze cloudomgeving beter leren kennen.

dutch: Mijn gevoel bij deze taak is positief.
english: I feel positive about this task.
scenario: A colleague asks how you feel about an assigned task. Explain that your overall feeling about it is positive.
cue: A colleague asks how you feel about an assigned task. Explain that your overall feeling about it is positive.
grammar: Present statement. The first constituent is Mijn gevoel bij deze taak; is is the finite main verb and Mijn gevoel bij deze taak is its subject. A normal declarative main clause has one first constituent and then its finite verb. The subject can be that first constituent. Other phrases can appear inside the verb bracket. Gevoel is a noun inside the subject Mijn gevoel bij deze taak. It is not the finite verb voel.
variation: Ik voel me zeker bij eenvoudige supportvragen.

dutch: Ik heb eerder met een soortgelijk ticketsysteem gewerkt.
english: I have previously worked with a similar ticketing system.
scenario: You are learning the team's request system. Explain to your mentor that you have worked with a similar system before.
cue: You are learning the team's request system. Explain to your mentor that you have worked with a similar system before.
grammar: Perfect and verb bracket. The first constituent is Ik; heb is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The finite auxiliary is in the main-clause verb position. Its object, pronouns and other phrases can stand before the participle that closes the bracket. Auxiliary choice depends on the actual verb and meaning. Soortgelijk means similar, not identical. The perfect reports experience without claiming mastery of the current system.
variation: Welke taken horen bij mijn rol als junior beheerder?

dutch: Welke vaardigheden heb ik voor deze rol vooral nodig?
english: Which skills do I especially need for this role?
scenario: You are planning how to develop in your new role. Ask your manager which skills are particularly important for it.
cue: You are planning how to develop in your new role. Ask your manager which skills are particularly important for it.
grammar: Question word and inversion. The first question constituent is Welke vaardigheden; heb is the finite verb. A question word/phrase comes first, then the finite verb and subject. In a subject question the question phrase itself is the subject, so no extra subject is needed. Welke vaardigheden is the object question phrase. Heb ... nodig is the need construction; vooral asks about emphasis.
variation: Mijn vorige team werkte met een ander meldingssysteem.

dutch: Ik weet dat ik nog veel over ons netwerk moet leren.
english: I know that I still have a lot to learn about our network.
scenario: During a learning review, acknowledge to your mentor that there is still a lot you need to learn about the team's network.
cue: During a learning review, acknowledge to your mentor that there is still a lot you need to learn about the team's network.
grammar: Main and subordinate clause. The first constituent is Ik; weet is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The main clause retains its own finite-verb position. The conjunction introduces a separate clause whose subject and other material precede its finite verb or verb group. The conjunction's meaning must fit the situation. Dat introduces known content. Ons belongs with singular het netwerk; moet leren is a final verb group.
variation: Ik heb er nog weinig ervaring mee.

dutch: Kan ik deze taak eerst samen met jou uitvoeren?
english: Can I carry out this task with you first?
scenario: You are about to perform an unfamiliar task. Ask your colleague informally whether you can do it together the first time.
cue: You are about to perform an unfamiliar task. Ask your colleague informally whether you can do it together the first time.
grammar: Modal request or permission question. The finite verb Kan comes before subject ik. The finite modal comes before the subject. The requested action stays an infinitive without te. Whether this asks about ability, permission or willingness depends on the actual modal and context. Samen met jou identifies collaboration, not handing the task over entirely. Eerst places the joint attempt before independent work.
variation: Ik weet hoe het team de documentatie bijwerkt.

dutch: Ik maak aantekeningen om de stappen later zelfstandig te herhalen.
english: I take notes so I can repeat the steps independently later.
scenario: A colleague is demonstrating a task to you. Explain that you are taking notes so that you can repeat the steps on your own later.
cue: A colleague is demonstrating a task to you. Explain that you are taking notes so that you can repeat the steps on your own later.
grammar: Purpose or intended action. The first constituent is Ik; maak is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. Om introduces an infinitive phrase with te. Its object can come before the infinitive; with a separable verb te stands between its particle and verb. This is not a second finite clause. The om te phrase expresses a learning purpose. Later distinguishes independent repetition from the current demonstration.
variation: Ik zal de serverdocumentatie deze week doornemen.

dutch: Ik werk twee dagen per week van thuis uit.
english: I work from home two days a week.
scenario: A colleague asks about your regular work arrangement. Explain that you work from home two days each week.
cue: A colleague asks about your regular work arrangement. Explain that you work from home two days each week.
grammar: Present statement. The first constituent is Ik; werk is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. A normal declarative main clause has one first constituent and then its finite verb. The subject can be that first constituent. Other phrases can appear inside the verb bracket. Van thuis uit is standard Belgian wording for working from home. The sentence states frequency without naming the days.
variation: Ik werk op vrijdag van thuis uit.

dutch: Op mijn thuiswerkdag ben ik via dezelfde chatgroep bereikbaar.
english: On my work-from-home day, I am reachable through the same chat group.
scenario: A teammate asks how to contact you while you work from home. Say that the same chat group can be used on that day.
cue: A teammate asks how to contact you while you work from home. Say that the same chat group can be used on that day.
grammar: Fronted phrase and V2. The first constituent is Op mijn thuiswerkdag; ben is the finite main verb and ik is its subject. The complete time, place or object phrase is one first constituent. The finite verb follows it, then the subject: second position means a constituent, not the second written word. The complete day phrase is first, so ben precedes ik. Dezelfde means the same rather than merely a similar group.
variation: Ik ben op mijn thuiswerkdag via dezelfde chatgroep bereikbaar.

dutch: Ik kom morgen naar kantoor omdat de nieuwe medewerker begeleiding nodig heeft.
english: I am coming to the office tomorrow because the new employee needs guidance.
scenario: Your colleague asks why you will be in the office tomorrow. Explain that the new employee needs guidance there.
cue: Your colleague asks why you will be in the office tomorrow. Explain that the new employee needs guidance there.
grammar: Main and subordinate clause. The first constituent is Ik; kom is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The main clause retains its own finite-verb position. The conjunction introduces a separate clause whose subject and other material precede its finite verb or verb group. The conjunction's meaning must fit the situation. Omdat gives a reason, not a condition. Nodig heeft closes the subordinate clause; tomorrow's visit is an arrangement.
variation: Ik kom naar kantoor als de gebruiker mijn hulp ter plaatse nodig heeft.

dutch: Ik ben thuis niet op het interne telefoonnummer bereikbaar.
english: I cannot be reached on the internal extension at home.
scenario: A colleague tries to use your internal extension while you work remotely. Explain that this number does not reach you at home.
cue: A colleague tries to use your internal extension while you work remotely. Explain that this number does not reach you at home.
grammar: Niet, geen and scope. The first constituent is Ik; ben is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. Geen negates an indefinite noun phrase or an uncountable amount. Niet negates a verb/state or another specific constituent. Nog niet means not yet; niet meer means no longer. The position depends on the intended scope. Niet negates reachability through that specific number. It does not say that every contact method is unavailable.
variation: Ik heb een rustige plek voor de ondersteuningsgesprekken ingericht.

dutch: Kunnen we de overdracht via een videogesprek doen?
english: Can we do the handover through a video call?
scenario: You and a colleague will be in different locations at shift change. Ask whether the handover can take place through a video call.
cue: You and a colleague will be in different locations at shift change. Ask whether the handover can take place through a video call.
grammar: Modal request or permission question. The finite verb Kunnen comes before subject we. The finite modal comes before the subject. The requested action stays an infinitive without te. Whether this asks about ability, permission or willingness depends on the actual modal and context. Kunnen expresses a proposed practical option. The question does not claim that a handover has already taken place.
variation: Ben je tijdens je thuiswerkdag op hetzelfde nummer bereikbaar?

dutch: Ik heb mijn thuiswerkdag met de teamleider afgestemd.
english: I have agreed my work-from-home day with the team leader.
scenario: A colleague asks whether your remote-work arrangement has been coordinated. Say that you have agreed the day with the team leader.
cue: A colleague asks whether your remote-work arrangement has been coordinated. Say that you have agreed the day with the team leader.
grammar: Perfect and verb bracket. The first constituent is Ik; heb is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. The finite auxiliary is in the main-clause verb position. Its object, pronouns and other phrases can stand before the participle that closes the bracket. Auxiliary choice depends on the actual verb and meaning. Afgestemd is the separable participle. Met identifies the person consulted; the statement concerns an agreed arrangement.
variation: We kunnen de overdracht ook op afstand bespreken.

dutch: Ik ben mijn thuiswerkplek aan het klaarmaken.
english: I am getting my home workstation ready.
scenario: Before starting a remote shift, a colleague asks what you are doing now. Explain that you are currently preparing your home workstation.
cue: Before starting a remote shift, a colleague asks what you are doing now. Explain that you are currently preparing your home workstation.
grammar: Ongoing activity with aan het. The first constituent is Ik; ben is the finite main verb and Ik is its subject. A finite form of zijn describes the ongoing state. Aan het is followed by an infinitive, not an extra finite verb. For separable verbs more than one progressive placement can be natural. Aan het klaarmaken describes preparation in progress. It does not imply the workstation is already ready.
variation: Ik heb thuis geen toegang tot de kantoorprinter.

dutch: Welke taken kunnen we even goed op afstand uitvoeren?
english: Which tasks can we carry out just as well remotely?
scenario: Your team is comparing remote and office work. Ask which tasks can be carried out equally well remotely.
cue: Your team is comparing remote and office work. Ask which tasks can be carried out equally well remotely.
grammar: Question word and inversion. The first question constituent is Welke taken; kunnen is the finite verb. A question word/phrase comes first, then the finite verb and subject. In a subject question the question phrase itself is the subject, so no extra subject is needed. Even goed means equally well, not briefly well. The question concerns practical suitability, not blanket permission.
variation: Gisteren werkten we vanuit verschillende kantoren.

dutch: Tijdens mijn vorige thuiswerkdag had ik regelmatig contact met de servicedesk.
english: During my previous work-from-home day, I had regular contact with the service desk.
scenario: Your manager asks about communication on your previous remote-working day. Report that you were in regular contact with the service desk.
cue: Your manager asks about communication on your previous remote-working day. Report that you were in regular contact with the service desk.
grammar: Simple past. The first constituent is Tijdens mijn vorige thuiswerkdag; had is the finite main verb and ik is its subject. The finite past form occupies the ordinary main-clause verb position. Its number agrees with the subject. The past event belongs to the context supplied, not automatically to every repeated or present situation. Had is singular past. Regelmatig means regularly; it does not mean continuously or on one specific channel.
variation: Laten we onze kantoordagen op elkaar afstemmen.

dutch: Als ik van locatie verander, werk ik mijn bereikbaarheid in de agenda bij.
english: When I change location, I update my contact availability in the calendar.
scenario: A teammate asks how they can find your current availability. Explain the routine you follow whenever you change work location.
cue: A teammate asks how they can find your current availability. Explain the routine you follow whenever you change work location.
grammar: Fronted subordinate clause. The first constituent is Als ik van locatie verander,; werk is the finite main verb and ik is its subject. The complete subordinate clause counts as the first constituent of the main clause. The main finite verb follows it, then the main subject. Inside the subordinate clause its own verb/group comes toward the end. The whole als-clause is the first constituent; werk follows before ik. Bijwerken splits as werk ... bij in the main clause.
variation: Ik ben de werkplek thuis aan het inrichten.
